newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Police say hunt for East Timor rebels continues.
newsitem.headline: Police say hunt for East Timor rebels continues.

text.p: Police said the hunt for separatist guerrillas continued on Tuesday in Indonesia's troubled East Timor territory, hit by the worst violence in years during last week's general election period.
At least 34 people died in attacks by separatists seeking to disrupt last Thursday's elections, in which Indonesia's ruling Golkar won a sweeping 74-percent of the vote nationwide.

"East Timor is generally quiet at the moment. We don't hear any reports of fresh clashes between the security forces and the guerrillas," a policeman told Reuters by telephone from the East Timor capital of Dili.
"The search for the guerrillas continues," he added without giving details.
In the most serious incident, separatists killed 16 policeman and a soldier in an ambush on Saturday morning as the group returned by truck after protecting election booths.
Another 17 people, including at least four rebels, died last Wednesday and Thursday in election-related violence, police said.
Indonesia occupied the former Portuguese colony in 1975 and annexed it the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
